title: High-resolution tactile observation makes hidden racket-control mechanisms learnable
abstract: arXiv:2610.35563v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Experts can master fine hand-object manipulation skills, yet limited conscious perception of rapid tactile interactions hinders their ability to articulate the underlying control mechanisms. Badminton racket control requires rapid, fine hand-force coordination, providing a demanding testbed for uncovering these mechanisms. An 864-node tactile-inertial glove with synchronized 100-Hz acquisition recorded over 14,000 strokes from more than 70 participants across five skills. Inspired by sensorimotor control, our mechanics-grounded two-layer framework inferred object-driving and grip-stabilizing control from tactile history, while resolving their spatiotemporal force realization. translated_title: 高分辨率触觉观测使隐藏的球拍控制机制变得可学习
translated_abstract: 专家能够掌握精细的手-物体操控技能，但对快速触觉交互的有限意识感知阻碍了他们清晰阐述潜在控制机制的能力。羽毛球拍控制需要快速而精细的手部力量协调，为揭示这些机制提供了一个高要求的测试平台。一款具有同步100 Hz采集能力的864节点触觉-惯性手套，记录了来自70多名参与者、覆盖五种技能水平的超过14,000次挥拍。受感觉运动控制启发，我们基于力学的双层框架从触觉历史中推断出驱动物体和稳定握持的控制，并解析了二者在时空上的力实现方式。我们发现更高的熟练程度与选择性而非广泛性的控制相关：表现为更强的技能特异性、预期性调节、局灶性远端调制以及更低的几何力矩抵消，而时空协调则呈现出非单调的
tldr: 通过864节点高分辨率触觉-惯性手套记录70余名不同水平参与者的14,000余次羽毛球挥拍，基于力学的双层框架分析表明，高超的球拍控制源于选择性而非广泛性的控制策略。
en_tdlr: Using an 864-node tactile-inertial glove to record over 14,000 badminton strokes from 70+ participants, a mechanics-grounded two-layer framework reveals that superior racket control stems from selective rather than extensive control strategies.
